newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Fire strikes again at Czech Litvinov refinery - CT.
newsitem.headline: Fire strikes again at Czech Litvinov refinery - CT.

text.p: The second fire in eight days struck the Ceska Rafinerska a.s. refinery near the northern Czech town of Litvinov, CTK news agency reported on Monday.

The latest fire broke out in the furnace of a cracking unit at about 9:30 pm local time on Sunday but was brought under control several hours later, the agency quoted a Ceska Rafinerska official as saying.
The fire started just hours after oil supplies were restored to the Litvinov refinery following a huge blaze last weekend.
It was not yet clear if supplies had been cut again to Litvinov, which is one of the two main Czech refineries.
Ceska Rafinerska officials were not immediately available for further comment.
An explosion on November 23 in the refinery's tanking station sparked a fire which was visible for several kilometres and sent dense smoke rolling into neighbouring Germany.

After the first fire, officials from Rafinerska, petrol companies, and the government determined that supplies at the second refinery at Kralupy and in the distribution network were sufficient for the short term, and it would not be necessary to tap state reserves.

In a deal completed last year, the IOC consortium of three foreign oil groups bought a 49 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska a.s., a company set up to operate the two refineries at Litvinov and Kralupy.
The IOC is equally owned by DuPont Co unit Conoco of the United States, Royal Dutch/Shell, and Italy's Agip SpA.
